newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sources say Swedish gov't negative to EMU - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sources say Swedish gov't negative to EMU - paper.

text.p: Sweden's Prime Minister Goran Persson and Finance Minister Erik Asbrink are negative to membership in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), according to party sources, the daily Svenska Dagbladet reported on Wednesday.
"One and a half months ago I understood that he (Persson) wasn't positive to EMU at all," a source told the newspaper.
"I was surprised because I thought everything concerned the timing of when it would suit Sweden to join, but that isn't the case."
"He is worried that Sweden will be a vassal state, that EMU will force us into such a situation," the source was quoted as saying.
Another source said that Persson sees the improvement of state finances as proof that Sweden can stand on its own feet.
Asbrink has said that he opposes EMU about 80 percent and favours it by around 20 percent, the newspaper said.
"If the two party heavyweights with the determining influence are against (EMU), it will be difficult to work for EMU," a source told the daily.
A source from the party top pointed out that the two ministers will not openly admit that they are against a Swedish EMU membership as they fear interest rates will rise.
The party board is due to present its view on EMU in the next few weeks, at the earliest next week, Svenska Dagbladet said.
"The wording will be woolly," a source was quoted as saying.
When Persson was Finance Minister, between September 1994 and March 1996, he was positive to EMU.
But then fears that EMU will turn into a federal union, removing power from member governments, made him turn negative, sources told Svenska Dagbladet.
